resolutions.researcher_notes: No source supports ProposalYear=2022. Evidence contradicts it: Shana/Petroenergy (en.shana.ir/news/227033, Oct 2014) reports IGAT-11 design was already COMPLETE in 2014; mizenaft.ir/news/27490 states the plan was initiated in 1390 (=2011) under Javad Owji's NIGC tenure. GlobalData's '2022' refers to an assumed CONSTRUCTION start, not the proposal. So the project was proposed ~2011 and designed by 2014, roughly a decade before 2022. ProposalYear should likely be 2011 (or 2014). CONTRADICTION FLAGGED. Left UNRESOLVED rather than cite a source for a value it disproves.

GlobalData headlines IGAT XI as the longest planned Middle East pipeline 'by 2026', supporting StartYear1=2026. CONFLICT: the same GlobalData analysis (as reprinted by worldpipelines.com/project-news/10012022/) states operation 'expected to start ... in 2025', and the underlying date is a GlobalData assumption, not an operator commitment. Single-origin (GlobalData; worldpipelines/pipeline-journal are reprints). Flagged 2025-vs-2026 discrepancy.

Capacity 110 MMSCMD corroborated by two independent Iranian sources plus GlobalData: Shana/Petroenergy (Oct 2014) '110 mcm/d of gas'; mizenaft.ir '110 میلیون متر مکعب گاز در روز'. GlobalData/worldpipelines independently state 110,000 mmcm/d. Consistent across all origins.

Length 1200 km corroborated by Shana/Petroenergy 2014 ('1200 kilometers') independently of GlobalData (worldpipelines reprint: '1200 km'). Minor discrepancy: mizenaft.ir cites the ORIGINAL design at ~1100 km with a proposed +~400 km rerouting, so length has varied with route changes; 1200 km is well supported for the current spec.
Diameter 56 in corroborated by Shana/Petroenergy 2014 ('56-inches') independently of GlobalData (worldpipelines: 'maximum diameter of 56 in.'). Consistent.

START = Asaluyeh, Bushehr: strongly corroborated (Shana 2014, mizenaft.ir, and GlobalData/worldpipelines all cite Asalouyeh origin). END = Bazargan, West Azerbaijan: single-origin (GlobalData via worldpipelines: 'from Asalouyeh ... through Ahvaz, Dehgolan, to the Bazargan'). CONTRADICTION FLAGGED: Shana's original 2014 design routed IGAT-11 through Bushehr/Fars/Yazd/Esfahan/Semnan to tie into the Tehran-Mashhad line (NOT to Bazargan), and mizenaft describes a later route change branching off IGAT-7. The Bazargan (NW border) terminus reflects the newer routing and rests on GlobalData alone; start is high-confidence, end is medium.

Cost USD 4 billion supported only by GlobalData ('estimated to cost 4 billion dollars'), reprinted by worldpipelines/pipeline-journal — one origin. No independent Iranian corroboration of the $4bn total found; mizenaft.ir only cites an incremental ~$2bn cost from the ~400 km reroute plus €1–1.8bn for extra compressors, which is a different figure. Single-origin, medium confidence.

Owner1=Iran Ministry of Petroleum 100% is a parent-level attribution: sources name the state operator, not the Ministry directly. worldpipelines/GlobalData: operator = National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC); Shana 2014: executed by Iranian Gas Engineering and Development Company (GEDC). Both NIGC and GEDC are wholly state-owned subsidiaries under Iran's Ministry of Petroleum, so 100% Ministry ownership is consistent, but the sources attribute the project to the subsidiary companies rather than naming the Ministry itself.
